questions.q: What motivates a good leader, according to Plutarch?
a: Honor and duty rather than applause
Wealth and the perks of high office
Power over rivals and critics
Fame and a lasting reputation
questions.why: Lesson one says a good leader is moved by honor and duty, not by a wish to receive acclaim.

questions.q: What happens when leaders are driven mainly by a desire for fame?
a: They act recklessly and destabilize society
They become cautious and slow to decide
They listen more closely to advisers
They retire earlier than other leaders
questions.why: Lesson one explains that glory-seeking leaders make immoderate choices and bring instability to the people they serve.

questions.q: How did Cato the Elder respond when Romans wanted to honor him with a statue?
a: He asked them not to put one up
He paid for a larger monument
He insisted it face the forum
He accepted only a small plaque
questions.why: Cato said he would rather people ask why he had no statue than why he had one, showing he cared little for reputation.

questions.q: What did Pericles use his speaking skill to achieve for Athens?
a: He kept the city out of wars
He raised taxes on wealthy citizens
He expanded the Athenian empire
He won a long campaign in Sicily
questions.why: Lesson two says Pericles persuaded Athens to avoid war and keep its prosperity, a peace that lasted through his life.

questions.q: What point does Plutarch draw from Aesop's fable of the fox and the ticks?
a: Replacing experienced leaders with novices endangers society
Leaders should remove all critics from office
Old leaders should retire to make room
Suffering quietly is better than seeking help
questions.why: Lesson three compares old leaders to the familiar ticks: their experience and moderation protect society from unstable newcomers.
